Watcom shadow-pointer walk (two-step form) — `pCVar5` is advanced into scratch `pCVar4`, then rebound via a later `pCVar5 = pCVar4;`. Functionally identical to the single-line self-update; replace `pCVar5->some_field[0]` reads with direct indexing on the original pointer and drop both the advance line and the rebind.

Ghidra pre-increment-array-walk loop artifact on `pCVar5` (per-iteration advance via struct-field/pointer arithmetic — single-var `pCVar5 = pCVar5;` self-assign, two-var `tmp = &pCVar5->field; pCVar5 = tmp;` ping-pong, or a bare `pCVar5 = pCVar5 + N;` advance followed by a `*pCVar5 =` store — plus a constant-index store on `pCVar5`). Watcom's advance-then-displaced-store (`ADD reg,N` / store `[reg + -N]`) loses the displacement here, so every store lands one element late and the first is never written. The stride/sentinel are baked from the original struct layout, so it overruns on any layout change (e.g. the 64-bit port). Always wrong as-decoded; cross-reference .asm and rewrite as a straightforward for-loop in a .keep (watch for the skip-row store-offset bug).
